newsitem.title: PHILIPPINES: PRESS DIGEST - Philippine newspapers - April 8.
newsitem.headline: PRESS DIGEST - Philippine newspapers - April 8.

text.p: These are the leading stories in Manila newspapers on Tuesday. Reuters has not verified these stories and does not vouch for their accuracy.
- Senator Raul Roco formally launched his bid for the presidency in his home town Naga city, Camarines Sur province. (BULLETIN/STAR)

- A 45-day nationwide gun ban will be implemented by the Philippine National Police starting on Saturday, April 12, in connection with the May 12 town elections, officials said yesterday. (ALL NEWSPAPERS)

- Fighting between government troops and some 100 Abu Sayyaf guerrillas entered its fourth day yesterday in the hinterlands of the Moslem-dominated town of Lantawan, Basilan province, the Armed Forces Southern Command reported yesterday. (STANDARD)

- The plan by the Philippine Central Bank to float $1.0 billion worth of Yankee bonds had been criticised by the Senate, claiming such a move could cost Filipino taxpayers a crunching 3 billion pesos worth in yearly interest payments. (TODAY)

- Securities and Exchange Commission chairman Perfecto Yasay has expressed alarm over rumours in the bourse that Megaworld Property and Holdings Inc was in financial distress, but ruled out a formal SEC investigation unless complainants showed up. (ALL NEWSPAPERS)

- San Miguel Corp chairman and chief executive officer Andres Soriano has launched a counter-offensive against plans by the Presidential Commission on Good Government (PCGG) to overthrow him from his post, sources said. The government is reportedly not too happy with the strategy taken by the conglomerate in the past years and this was reflected in its poor earnings performance last year. (INQUIRER)
